soap_text:
Chief Complaint
Annual wellness visit and routine health review.

History of Present Illness
The patient presents for a scheduled Medicare wellness visit and routine annual health review. Preventive screenings, health risk assessment, medications, functional status, cognition, mood, fall risk, vaccine status, and personalized prevention planning were reviewed. The patient reports feeling well today and does not raise a new concern. The primary care clinician documents that this practice remains the continuing focal point for the patient's health needs and care coordination.

The patient also has longstanding atrial fibrillation after prior ablation. Cardiology records were reviewed during wellness planning. Anticoagulation was discussed but deferred today because the patient has had recurrent falls and bruising risk. Stroke and bleeding risk will be reassessed at follow-up.

Review of Systems
General: Feeling well. Cardiovascular: No chest pain or palpitations. Respiratory: No shortness of breath. Neurologic: No dizziness reported; history of recurrent falls reviewed in risk planning.

Physical Exam
BP 122/76, HR 68, SpO2 98%, BMI 26.1.
General: Well appearing, no acute distress. Heart: Regular rate and rhythm. Lungs: Clear to auscultation. Gait steady.

Assessment/Plan
1. Subsequent Medicare Annual Wellness Visit | (Z00.00: Encounter for general adult medical examination without abnormal findings)
Health risk assessment reviewed. Personalized prevention plan updated. Age-appropriate screening schedule and vaccine counseling discussed. Medication list and care team reviewed.

2. Routine adult preventive health examination | (Z00.00: Encounter for general adult medical examination without abnormal findings)
Routine annual preventive exam completed. Continue healthy diet, regular activity, and routine annual follow-up.

3. Atrial fibrillation after prior ablation | (I48.91: Unspecified atrial fibrillation)
Risk plan reviewed in the context of fall risk and bruising risk. Anticoagulation was discussed and deferred with risk-based reasoning. Reassess stroke and bleeding risk at follow-up.

4. Longitudinal primary care visit complexity
The clinician documents ongoing primary care responsibility as the continuing focal point for all needed services, including coordination of preventive screening, medication list maintenance, care team updates, chronic-care risk review, and annual follow-up planning.
